mechanism_narrative: A 2% quarterly increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strengthening economic growth, leading to increased consumer spending and, subsequently, higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 50% of quarters with 2%+ GDPC1 growth.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 1.5%, signaling tightening monetary policy, S&P 500 forward returns tend to decline over the next 20 trading days due to increased borrowing costs.
failure_condition: 20-day forward SPX returns remain positive in > 70% of instances with FEDFUNDS above 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Jointly, when UNRATE falls below 6% and PAYEMS increases by 0.5% in a month, the strengthening labor market indicates increased consumer power, driving S&P 500 returns higher over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward SPX returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances with the specified labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A 1.2% monthly increase in INDPRO, indicating a surge in industrial production, precedes increased demand for raw materials and, consequently, higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) increases by 1% in a month, signaling robust consumer spending, and concurrently HOUST (housing starts) rises by 5%, indicating a strong housing market, S&P 500 returns are likely to increase over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward SPX returns are negative in > 30% of instances with the specified demand conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in CPIAUCSL (consumer price index) by 0.5% in two months, indicating easing inflation pressures, leads to decreased expectations of future interest rate hikes, resulting in higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward SPX returns do not significantly outperform baseline (t-test p > 0.1) in periods with easing inflation.

mechanism_narrative: Always, the level of UNRATE (unemployment rate) provides a baseline indicator of economic health; when below 7%, it consistently correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward SPX returns are negative in > 45% of instances with UNRATE below 7%.

mechanism_narrative: In the regime of early-cycle recovery, a 2% increase in GDPC1 (GDP) within a quarter, coupled with a 1% increase in RSAFS (retail sales) within a month, jointly predict increased economic activity, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward SPX returns in early-cycle recoveries with the specified conditions are not significantly higher than in other regimes (t-test p > 0.05).
